description:
The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and employs a linear scale extending from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The first line, representing “Final Accuracy”, is blue with circular markers connected by a solid line; it begins at approximately 0.87 with associated error bars, plateaus around 0.93, and ends at approximately 0.91 with associated error bars. The second line, representing “Δ Accuracy”, is orange with diamond markers connected by a dashed line; it begins at approximately 0.26 with error bars, declines to approximately 0.17 at 0.92, and ends at approximately 0.24 with associated error bars. Lastly, the third line, representing “Initial Accuracy”, is green with square markers connected by a dotted line; it begins at approximately 0.74 with error bars, increases to approximately 0.83 at 0.94, and ends at approximately 0.80 with associated error bars.
